body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāse.
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāsa</s> (Squirrels' Feeding Ground).

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat. adrākṣīd āyuṣmān ānando rājagṛhe nagare sāvadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāṇo 'nyatamasmin pradeśe kūṭāgāram aśītidvāram ulliptāvaliptam ucchṛtadhvajapatākam āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpam. dṛṣṭvā ca punas tasyaitad abhavat. yaḥ kaścic chrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā īdṛśaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ kārayitvā caturdiśe bhikṣusaṃghe niryātayed yo vā tathāgatasyārhatḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāmalakapramāṇaṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet sūcīmātrāṃ yaṣṭim āropayed badarīpatramātraṃ cchatraṃ yavaphalapramāṇāṃ pratimāṃ kārayet sarṣaphalapramāṇaṃ dhātuṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet tat katamaṃ tataḥ prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ syāt? athāyuṣmata ānandasyaitad abhavat. śāstā me saṃmukhībhūtaḥ sugato me saṃmukhībhūtaḥ. yaṇv aham etam evārthaṃ bhagavata ārocayeyaṃ yathā me sa bhagavāṃ vyākariṣyati tathāhaṃ dhārayiṣyāmīty.
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having dressed in the forenoon and taken up his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. While carefully going about for alms in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> saw in a certain place a mansion with eighty doors, plastered inside and outside, with raised banners and flags, adorned with silk ribbons and garland-clusters. Having seen it, this thought occurred to him: "If some faithful son of good family or daughter of good family were to have such a mansion built and offer it to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks) of the four directions, or if someone were to erect a <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary mound) the size of an <s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan) fruit for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, and raise upon it a pole the size of a needle, and place upon it a parasol the size of a <s>badarī</s> (jujube) leaf, and have an image made the size of a barley grain, and install a relic the size of a mustard seed — which of these two would produce the greater merit?" Then this thought occurred to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "The Teacher is present before me, the Well-Gone One is present before me. Let me report this very matter to the Blessed One; as the Blessed One declares, so shall I retain it."

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānando rājagṛhe nagare sāvadānaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtya paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratiśamayya pādau prakṣālya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt. ekāntasthita āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat. ihāhaṃ bhadanta pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣaṃ. so 'ham adrākṣam rājagṛhe nagare sāvadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāṇo 'nyatamasmin pradeśe kūṭāgāram aśītidvāram ulliptāvaliptam ucchṛtadhvajapatākam āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā ca punar me etad abhavat. yaḥ kaścic chrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā īdṛśaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ caturdiśe bhikṣusaṃghe niryātayed yo vā tathāgatasyārhatḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya mṛttikāpiṇḍād āmalakapramāṇaṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet sūcīmātrāṃ yaṣṭim āropayed badarīpatramātraṃ cchatraṃ yavaphalapramāṇāṃ pratimāṃ kārayet sarṣaphalapramāṇaṃ dhātuṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet tat katamaṃ tataḥ prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ syāt? tasya mamaitad abhavat. śāstā me saṃmukhībhūtaḥ sugato me saṃmukhībhūtaḥ. yanv aham etam evārthaṃ bhagavata ārocayeyaṃ yathā bhagavāṃ vyākariṣyati tathāhaṃ dhārayiṣyāmīty.
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having carefully gone about for alms in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, having finished his meal, having returned from his alms-round after eating, having put away his bowl and robe, having washed his feet, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Here, Venerable Sir, having dressed in the forenoon and taken up my bowl and robe, I entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. While carefully going about for alms in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, I saw in a certain place a mansion with eighty doors, plastered inside and outside, with raised banners and flags, adorned with silk ribbons and garland-clusters. Having seen it, this thought occurred to me: 'If some faithful son of good family or daughter of good family were to offer such a mansion to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> of the four directions, or if someone were to erect a <s>stūpa</s> the size of an <s>āmalaka</s> fruit from a lump of clay for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and raise upon it a pole the size of a needle, and place upon it a parasol the size of a <s>badarī</s> leaf, and have an image made the size of a barley grain, and install a relic the size of a mustard seed — which of these two would produce the greater merit?' Then this thought occurred to me: 'The Teacher is present before me, the Well-Gone One is present before me. Let me report this very matter to the Blessed One; as the Blessed One declares, so shall I retain it.'"

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānanda, idam avocat. sādhu sādhv ānanda bahujanahitāya tvam ānanda pratipanno ca bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai arthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇāṃ yas tvaṃ tathāgatam etam evārthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase. tena hy ānanda śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru, bhāṣiṣye. jambūdvīpo hy ānanda dvīpaḥ saptayojanasahasrāṇy āyāmavistāreṇa uttaraviśālo dakṣiṇena śakaṭāmukhaḥ tam enam kāscic chrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā saptaratnamayaṃ kṛtvā srotāpannebhyaḥ sakṛdāgāmibhyo 'nāgāmibhyo 'rhadbhyaḥ pratyekabuddhebhyaś cāturdiśe vā bhkiṣusaṃghe niryātayet. yo vā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyakasaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya mṛttikāpiṇḍād āmalakaphalapramāṇaṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet sūcīmātrāṃ vā yaṣṭim āropayet badarīpatramātracchattram yavaphalapramāṇaṃ pratimāṃ kārayet sarṣaphalapramāṇaṃ dhātuṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet, idam evānanda tataḥ prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ vadāmi.
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Well done, well done, <s>Ānanda</s>! You, <s>Ānanda</s>, have acted for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans, in that you think fit to ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> this very matter. Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, listen well and attend carefully; I shall speak. <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (the Rose-Apple Continent), O <s>Ānanda</s>, is seven thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth, broad in the north and shaped like a cart's face in the south. If some faithful son of good family or daughter of good family were to make it all of the seven precious substances and offer it to <s>Srotāpannas</s> (stream-enterers), <s>Sakṛdāgāmins</s> (once-returners), <s>Anāgāmins</s> (non-returners), <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), or the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> of the four directions — or if someone were to erect a <s>stūpa</s> the size of an <s>āmalaka</s> fruit from a lump of clay for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and raise upon it a pole the size of a needle, and place upon it a parasol the size of a <s>badarī</s> leaf, and have an image made the size of a barley grain, and install a relic the size of a mustard seed — I declare, O <s>Ānanda</s>, that this latter produces the greater merit."

body.text: tiṣṭhatv ānanda jambūdvīpo dvīpaḥ. asty ānanda pūrvavideho nāma dvīpo 'ṣṭauyojanasahasrāṇy āyāmavistāreṇa samantād ardhacandrākārapariṇāmitaḥ. tam enaṃ kaścit śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā saptaratnamayaṃ kṛtvā cāturdiśe bhkiṣusaṃghe niryātayet yo vā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyakasaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛttasya mṛtpiṇḍād āmalakaphalapramāṇaṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet sūcīmātrāṃ yaṣṭim āropayed badarīpatramātraṃ cchattram yavaphalapramāṇaṃ pratimāṃ kārayet sarṣaphalapramāṇaṃ dhātuṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet idam evānanda tataḥ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ vadāmi.
body.translated_text: Let the continent of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> be set aside, O <s>Ānanda</s>. There is, O <s>Ānanda</s>, a continent called <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, eight thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth in every direction, shaped like a half-moon. If some faithful son of good family or daughter of good family were to make it all of the seven precious substances and offer it to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks) of the four directions, or if someone were to erect a <s>stūpa</s> the size of an <s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan) fruit from a lump of clay for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and raise upon it a pole the size of a needle, and place upon it a parasol the size of a <s>badarī</s> (jujube) leaf, and have an image made the size of a barley grain, and install a relic the size of a mustard seed — I declare, O <s>Ānanda</s>, that this latter produces even greater merit than that.

body.text: tiṣṭhatv ānanda jambūdvīpo dvīpaḥ. asty ānandāvaragodānīyo nāma dvīpo navayojanasahasrāṇy āyāmavistāreṇa samantāt pūrṇacandrākārapariṇāmitaḥ. tam enaṃ kaścic chrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā saptaratnamayaṃ kṛtvā yāvac cāturdiśe bhkiṣusaṃghe niryātayed yo vā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyakasaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛttasya mṛtpiṇḍād āmalakaphalapramāṇaṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet sūcīmātrāṃ yaṣṭim āropayed badarīpatramātraṃ cchattram yavaphalapramāṇaṃ pratimāṃ kārayet sarṣaphalapramāṇaṃ dhātuṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet idam evānanda tataḥ prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ vadāmi.
body.translated_text: Let the continent of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> be set aside, O <s>Ānanda</s>. There is, O <s>Ānanda</s>, a continent called <s>Avaragodānīya</s>, nine thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth in every direction, shaped like a full moon. If some faithful son of good family or daughter of good family were to make it all of the seven precious substances and offer it to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> of the four directions, or if someone were to erect a <s>stūpa</s> the size of an <s>āmalaka</s> fruit from a lump of clay for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and raise upon it a pole the size of a needle, and place upon it a parasol the size of a <s>badarī</s> leaf, and have an image made the size of a barley grain, and install a relic the size of a mustard seed — I declare, O <s>Ānanda</s>, that this latter produces even more abundant merit than that.

body.text: tiṣṭhatv ānanda jambūdvīpo dvīpaḥ. tiṣṭhatu pūrvavideho dvīpaḥ. tiṣṭhatv avaragodānīyo dvīpaḥ. asty ānanda uttarakurur nāma dvīpaḥ daśayojanasahasrāṇy āyāmavistāreṇa samantāt samantacaturasraḥ. tam enaṃ kaścic chrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā saptaratnamayaṃ kṛtvā yāvac cāturdiśe bhkiṣusaṃghe niryātayed yo vā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyakasaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛttasya mṛtpiṇḍād āmalakaphalapramāṇaṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet sūcīmātrāṃ yaṣṭim āropayed badarīpatramātraṃ cchattram yavaphalapramāṇaṃ pratimāṃ kārayet sarṣaphalapramāṇaṃ dhātuṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet tataḥ prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ vadāmi.
body.translated_text: Let the continent of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> be set aside, O <s>Ānanda</s>. Let the continent of <s>Pūrvavideha</s> be set aside. Let the continent of <s>Avaragodānīya</s> be set aside. There is, O <s>Ānanda</s>, a continent called <s>Uttarakuru</s>, ten thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth in every direction, perfectly square in all directions. If some faithful son of good family or daughter of good family were to make it all of the seven precious substances and offer it to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> of the four directions, or if someone were to erect a <s>stūpa</s> the size of an <s>āmalaka</s> fruit from a lump of clay for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and raise upon it a pole the size of a needle, and place upon it a parasol the size of a <s>badarī</s> leaf, and have an image made the size of a barley grain, and install a relic the size of a mustard seed — I declare that this latter produces even more abundant merit than that.

body.text: tiṣṭhatv ānanda jambūdvīpo dvīpas. tiṣṭhatu pūrvavideho dvīpaḥ. tiṣṭhatv avaragodānīyo dvīpaḥ. tiṣṭhatūttarakuru dvīpaḥ. asty ānanda śakrasya devānām indrasya vaijayanto nāma prāsādaḥ. tam enaṃ kaścic chrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā saptaratnamayaṃ kṛtvā yāvac cāturdiśe bhkiṣusaṃghe niryātayed yo vā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyakasaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛttasya mṛtpiṇḍād āmalakaphalapramāṇaṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet sūcīmātrāṃ yaṣṭim āropayed badarīpatramātraṃ cchattram yavaphalapramāṇaṃ pratimāṃ kārayet sarṣaphalapramāṇaṃ dhātuṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet idam evānanda tataḥ prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ vadāmi.
body.translated_text: Let the continent of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> be set aside, O <s>Ānanda</s>. Let the continent of <s>Pūrvavideha</s> be set aside. Let the continent of <s>Avaragodānīya</s> be set aside. Let the continent of <s>Uttarakuru</s> be set aside. There is, O <s>Ānanda</s>, a palace called <s>Vaijayanta</s> belonging to <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods. If some faithful son of good family or daughter of good family were to make it all of the seven precious substances and offer it to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> of the four directions, or if someone were to erect a <s>stūpa</s> the size of an <s>āmalaka</s> fruit from a lump of clay for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and raise upon it a pole the size of a needle, and place upon it a parasol the size of a <s>badarī</s> leaf, and have an image made the size of a barley grain, and install a relic the size of a mustard seed — I declare, O <s>Ānanda</s>, that this latter produces even more abundant merit than that.

body.text: tiṣṭhatv ānanda jambūdvīpo dvīpaḥ. tiṣṭhatu pūrvavideho dvīpaḥ. tiṣṭhatv avaragodānīyo dvīpaḥ. tiṣṭhatūttarakuru dvīpaḥ. tiṣṭhatu śakrasya devānām indrasya vaijayantaḥ prāsādaḥ. asty ānanda trisāharsamahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ. tam enaṃ kaścic chrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā saptaratnamayaṃ kṛtvā srotāpannebhyaḥ sakṛdāgāmibhyo 'nāgāmibhyo 'rhadbhyaḥ pratyekabuddhebhyaś yāvac cāturdiśe vā bhkiṣusaṃghe niryātayed yo vā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyakasaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛttasya mṛtpiṇḍād āmalakaphalapramāṇaṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet sūcīmātrāṃ yaṣṭim āropayed badarīpatramātraṃ cchattram yavaphalapramāṇaṃ pratimāṃ kārayet sarṣaphalapramāṇaṃ dhātuṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet idam evānanda tataḥ prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ vadāmi.
body.translated_text: Set aside <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, O <s>Ānanda</s>. Set aside <s>Pūrvavideha</s> (the Eastern Continent). Set aside <s>Avaragodānīya</s> (the Western Continent). Set aside <s>Uttarakuru</s> (the Northern Continent). Set aside the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods. There exists, O <s>Ānanda</s>, the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>). If some faithful son of good family or daughter of good family were to make it entirely of the seven precious substances and offer it to <s>Srotāpannas</s> (stream-enterers), <s>Sakṛdāgāmins</s> (once-returners), <s>Anāgāmins</s> (non-returners), <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), and even to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> of the four directions — or if someone were to erect a <s>stūpa</s> the size of an <s>āmalaka</s> fruit from a lump of clay for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and raise upon it a pole the size of a needle, and place upon it a parasol the size of a <s>badarī</s> leaf, and have an image made the size of a barley grain, and install a relic the size of a mustard seed — I declare, O <s>Ānanda</s>, that this latter produces the greater merit.

body.text: tat kasya hetoḥ. aprameyo hy ānanda tathāgato dānenāprameyaḥ śīlenāprameyaḥ kṣāntyāprameyo vīryeṇāprameyo tyāgenāprameyo maitryāprameyaḥ karuṇayāprameyo muditayāprameya upekṣayā caturbhir vaiśāradyais daśabhis tathāgatabalaiś aṣṭādaśabhir āveṇikair buddhadharmair aprameyāprameyaguṇasamanvāgato hy ānanda tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ.
body.translated_text: For what reason? Because, O <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is immeasurable in generosity, immeasurable in moral discipline, immeasurable in patience, immeasurable in vigor, immeasurable in renunciation, immeasurable in loving-kindness, immeasurable in compassion, immeasurable in sympathetic joy, immeasurable in equanimity, (immeasurable) in the four confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), in the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), and in the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>). The <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one is indeed endowed with immeasurable, immeasurable virtues, O <s>Ānanda</s>.

body.text: evam ukto āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat: āścaryaṃ bhagavann āścaryaṃ sugata yāvad ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ. ko nāmāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ. kathaṃ cainaṃ dhārayāmi. tasmāt tarhi tvam ānanda imaṃ dharmaparyāyam adbhutam adbhutadharmaparyāyaṃ iti dhāraya. idam avocad bhagavān āttamanās te bhikṣava āyuṣmāṃś cānando bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan.
body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "It is wondrous, O Blessed One! It is wondrous, O Well-Gone One, how great this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma) is! What is the name of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>? And how shall I retain it?" "Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should retain this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> as 'The Wondrous' — the <s>Adbhutadharmaparyāya</s> (Discourse on the Wondrous Dharma)." Thus spoke the Blessed One. Those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with joyful minds, rejoiced in the words spoken by the Blessed One.
